fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain clear vehicle width for emergency apparatus.
• Cut back dense vegetation that crowds the sides of the access drive to prevent it from blocking a responder's view of the main residence on approach.
• Trim shrubs and low-hanging branches near the main residence and detached structure to create clear ground-level movement around both buildings.
• Keep a clear path between the detached structure and the main residence so responders can move between buildings without pushing through vegetation.
• Mark or post the single driveway entrance clearly so incoming units can identify it without slowing to search.
• Keep the walkway and patio area clear of stored items so responders can move around the building perimeter without obstruction.
• Install a secondary access point or gate at the rear of the property if the lot boundary and yard layout allow, reducing dependence on the single front access point.
• If a rear gate exists, keep it unlocked and mark it visibly so responders can reach the rear of the property without returning to the front.
• Thin dense vegetation at the rear of the property to allow responders on foot to move along the back of the main residence and detached structure.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to create open space between individual trees and the building.
• Trim branches on large trees that extend over or directly toward the roof and walls.
• Remove shrubs and low plants growing immediately against the exterior walls of the structure.
• Thin vegetation growing between structures so fire cannot easily move from one building to the next.
• Clear brush from the area identified near the property to reduce the amount of burnable material close to structures.
• Mow or cut down ground vegetation around structures, especially within the nearest several feet of exterior walls.
• Trim overhanging branches along the single access route so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep the driveway surface and shoulders clear of fallen branches, dead leaves, and overgrown vegetation.
• Clear vegetation and debris from the rear of the property to allow movement around the back of the structure.
• Remove dead wood, dry leaves, and accumulated plant debris from under large trees near the structure.
• Separate scattered trees from nearby shrubs and ground plants so there is open ground between them and the building.
• Maintain the existing open separation between vegetation and structures by keeping it clear of new growth and debris.
